nodes.line: Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

This is going to sound small. I am sending back 74 papers a day from Campsie and paying to have them collected, which is a business model somebody invented on purpose. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Do not make a scene about it.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. They will drop my Campsie order if I can show $142 of turnover on the other side of the shop by the week of the show. This is the third time I have had this conversation. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

choices.text: The Better Rate, Campsie — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

Do not laugh. I do the Campsie round from the middle of the news and for the last fortnight somebody has been taking the papers off the front steps behind me. It started small, the way these things do. Come back and tell me straight.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. There is a dog on the Campsie round that has had two of my bags and an esky with no lid that was not even mine. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do that and we're square.
Go on then. What did you find.

choices.text: The Dog on Ash Street, Campsie — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
If you are selling something the answer is no.

Two people have already said no. Nine of us at Campsie have gone in on the same numbers since the week of the show and one of us has stopped putting money in. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. The agency at Belmore closed six months before Campsie started struggling, and I would very much like to know what they know. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do not let them talk you into anything.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: The Other Agency, Campsie — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Alina, panel beater at Castle Hill

nodes.line: Cash only and no, I am joking. What do you want.

This is going to sound small. There has been a car in the Castle Hill yard since a wet Monday with a docket book on the passenger seat and no owner answering. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Do not make a scene about it.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. Now that it is documented, Castle Hill is owed $136 in storage and the only person who can pay it is the person not answering. This is the third time I have had this conversation. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Right. Tell me and do not soften it.

choices.text: The Unclaimed Falcon, Castle Hill — that's done.
Storage Fees, Castle Hill — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
You have got a face like you can keep your mouth shut.
Do not laugh. I am in my first year at Castle Hill and I have to log 67 hours on a job I am not allowed to touch on my own. It started small, the way these things do. Come back and tell me straight.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Somebody has been coming into the Castle Hill yard after two in the afternoon to use the air line, and last week they used the compressor as well. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do that and we're square.
I have been thinking about it all day. Out with it.

choices.text: First Year, Castle Hill — that's done.
The Air Line, Castle Hill — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Elin, the bloke whose car it is at Castle Hill

nodes.line: Right. Talk while I do this.

Two people have already said no. My car has been at Castle Hill since a wet Monday and every time I ring, the quote has grown by about $67. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. The insurance assessor who signs off every job at Castle Hill works out of Hills Showground, and he has never once seen the car he is assessing. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do not let them talk you into anything.
Well? I can read your face from here.

choices.text: My Own Car, Castle Hill — that's done.
The Assessor, Castle Hill — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
You right there? I am mid-something but go on.

This is going to sound small. People leave things at the Gymea roller door after two in the afternoon and by morning it is rained on and it is our problem and our tip fee. Everyone I have told has looked at me the way you are now. Do not make a scene about it.

I have written it down twice and lost it twice. The photos worked, which means Gymea can claim back the $42 we have paid to throw away other people's furniture since a Tuesday. This is the third time I have had this conversation. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: Dumped Out the Back, Gymea — that's done.
The Tip Fee, Gymea — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
If you are here about the sign, the sign is wrong.

Do not laugh. Something came into Gymea on a Tuesday in a box of paperbacks that I do not think the family meant to give away. It started small, the way these things do. Come back and tell me straight.

It is the sort of thing you notice or you do not. Two people have been coming into the Gymea sorting room since a Tuesday and taking the good stock before it reaches the floor, and one of them volunteers here. It is the not knowing that has got me, honestly. Do that and we're square.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

choices.text: The Good Box, Gymea — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Don't stand in the doorway, mate, come round.

Two people have already said no. I do the Gymea pick-ups in a van with 31 thousand on it and a door that only opens if you know about it. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. I will owe you one, and I pay those.

Someone has to, and it may as well be you. Everything Gymea cannot sell goes to a warehouse at Kirrawee, and nobody there has ever answered a phone in my hearing. You will see what I mean the second you get there. Do not let them talk you into anything.
Before you start: did anyone see you.
No dramas. Come back when you are bored.
